title: Best clarinetists in New Orleans; Piku and Robichaux's band
summary: He names Joe Watson and others as best players and discusses Piku's reading and jazz playing.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Yes. When you got to New Orleans, who was the best down at play in town next to you?

Well, no, that's kind of a whole dance. That's a loaded question. Yeah, because I still like Joe Watson to my idea. Then there was Zell, he was with Redhead, yeah, he was with Redhead, he was supposed to beat him. Oh, yeah. Then there was Piku, Teo, all those guys, man.
Did Piku play much jazz in those days?
Well, yeah, when he come in he started playing a jazz.
He wasn't playing with the reading bands much then, huh?
Well, yeah, he played with John Robeshow when he was down in that pit. Uh-huh. And he had to read the state on that pit.
And he played some jazz too at the same, on the same job? Yeah. Yeah. With Robeshow? Yeah.
He played with some of the late hotels and things, right?
No, but I mean, would they put you in the alley, that band?

Well, yeah, they did flash a number every now and then. Uh-huh. The old man John, he was strictly, he watched that stuff. He didn't like to flash too much. He didn't feature nobody but Happy around there all the time, on the drums.

He was the only one that would really get going, huh? Yeah, really kick out there. Redhead? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. So, I don't know. Um, everything well we get there. Oh, that's the Tutt Johnson band, yeah.
